page: OVHcloud t2-180 is a high-density GPU server engineered for demanding machine learning inference, distributed model training, and heavy compute workloads. Operating under the KVM hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture, the instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6226R processors running at a base clock of 2.9 GHz. The compute topology features 60 physical cores with hyperthreading disabled, delivering 60 dedicated execution threads accompanied by AVX-512 vector extensions. The platform includes 180 GB of system RAM, allocating 3.0 GB per physical core, paired with a bundled 4050 GB local NVMe SSD for high-speed local scratch space and dataset caching. Networking is supported by a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth profile, though complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Hardware acceleration is anchored by four discrete NVIDIA Volta V100S GPUs providing 128 GB of combined VRAM (32 GB per accelerator). In synthetic testing, this GPU cluster demonstrates top-tier large language model inference capability, registering 15,326.13 tokens per second on prompt processing for 135M models and 1,355.49 tokens per second on 7B models. Text generation throughput remains robust, maintaining 121.32 tokens per second on 7B parameter architectures. On the host processor, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 310.34 GB per second and PassMark extended instruction routines achieve 51,664.44 points, reflecting solid vector processing performance. General CPU benchmarks such as Geekbench multi-core (10,599.0) and stress-ng multi-core (60,250.06) land within standard mid-range operational tiers.

The architectural balance of t2-180 favors workloads requiring simultaneous GPU acceleration and direct local disk input/output. By combining quad V100S GPUs with 4050 GB of integrated NVMe storage, the system avoids external network disk bottlenecks during large batch reads. Because each core is a dedicated physical unit without simultaneous multithreading, compute contention is eliminated, though raw per-core frequency is moderate compared to modern single-socket platforms. Qualitative cost efficiency is driven by the dense aggregation of four Enterprise-grade GPUs, extensive NVMe capacity, and dedicated core counts within a single virtual machine boundary. The platform is strategically suited for transformer-based inference serving, deep learning fine-tuning, high-throughput image processing, and distributed simulation pipelines.

Benchmark results reflect top-tier LLM inference execution, reaching 15,326 tokens per second on 135M prompt evaluation and 1,355 tokens per second on 7B models.
